paragraphs: Last month, the Explorers went to the nature park with Ranger Mark. He showed them many butterflies and told them about the tall trees. Now the children wanted to say thank you. Leo made a poster for the club on Monday. He drew it on big green paper. He wrote the words with a black pen. Lily put it on the wall next to the library door. Teacher Kim read it and said, "It is ready."

This is what the poster said. "EXPLORERS' CARD DAY!" "Make a thank you card for Ranger Mark." "Day: Thursday." "Time: one o'clock, and we finish at half past two." "Place: the school library, across the field from the hall." "Bring: scissors and colored paper." "The library has wifi, so we can look at photos of the park." "Teacher Kim helps everyone with the cutting."

Mia read the poster after lunch. "We usually read books in the club hour," she said. "This week we make cards, and I like that idea." Leo smiled at his poster. "I decided to draw a small tiger on my card," he said. "Ranger Mark likes all animals, so he can have a tiger."

That evening, Mia sent a message to May. "Hi May, this is Mia. I have just looked at Leo's poster again. Card Day is on Thursday at one o'clock in the school library. The library is across the field from the hall, so we can walk there after lunch. Please bring your scissors and some colored paper. Have you decided what to write for Ranger Mark? I want to say thank you for the butterflies. See you on Thursday! Mia"
May answered in two minutes. "Thank you, Mia. I have my scissors, and I am ready. I want to say thank you for the tall trees. See you in the library!"
